Strikethrough text ([strike] example [/strike]) means a point is no longer valid as of the most recent update and will be removed soon. Please let me know if I missed something. [b] Bold [/b] means something new from the most recent update.

Here are some things that I feel are important to know and/or that I wanted to know before I bought this game:

MOST IMPORTANT: This game currently does *not* have cloud saves. So if you're playing on PC and want to play on your steam deck, prepare to start all over again. This is by far the biggest negative i've found with this game yet. [b] Going off the 1.09 patchnotes, this will be addressed soon [/b]

Other things:

• There is no voice chat. (this can be a positive or negative depending on player)
• There can be up to 12 players in a server. [b] You can now make the max player count lower when setting up a server. [/b]
• The fishing minigame requires rapid mouse clicking. [b] There is an autoclicker that can be enabled in the settings to help with this. [/b]
• Servers are hosted by players for free. If the host disconnects, the whole server closes.
• There are 4 settings for server privacy: Public, Code-only, [b]Friends-only[/b] and Offline/Solo. Anyone in a public or code lobby can obtain or share the code to share with others. The lobby code is a 6 digit code for example "FOU2HR".
• [b] You can mark your server as "18+". This doesn't change anything gameplay wise, but it is shown on the server listing as well as making a pop-up appear for players who join your server that they need to accept. [/b]
• There is no lobby descriptions, what you can see before you join is: the host's name and the playercount, formatted as "TheQuackinator4's Lobby [4/12]" [b] You can change the server name as well as of 1.09, as well as being able to see if the host has set the server to 18+. [/b]
• The host can kick or ban players
• You can mute and hide players
• Players can punch eachother, including into the water. This can be disabled for you in the settings.
• The game chat seems to have a similar culture to MMOs, for better or worse. The public lobbies are very much not for younger and/or more sensitive players.
• Adding on to the previous point, as the "mature content description" on the steam page mentions, the game itself contains some mild swearing and jokes that wouldn't be appropriate for younger players.
• While the game doesn't seem to save between devices, if you leave or are removed from a server, any progress you made on that server does save on that device, so you don't need to worry about restarting every time
• You can draw and erase stuff in certain areas of the game, including being able to draw over and erase other players' drawings.
• If you don't use a code, the public servers you join/host seem to be in your region, as practically all players I've encountered in public servers turned out to be in Denmark, which I am too. So your experience with other players may dramatically depend on where you're located. I don't know how locally it matches players with you, whether it's in the same country or near where you live.
• [strike] This game keeps ALL chat history from your current session and will not delete any chat history until you close and reopen the game. After alot of chatting, I've found that interacting with the chat window makes the game slow to a crawl and the chat scroll bar becomes like, one pixel tall. I do not know if there's a way to delete chat history without restarting the game. [/strike]

Have any more things you want to know before you buy the game?

As a bonus tip as a thank you for reading this review, type "[b] /wag [/b]" in chat.

I picked this up very impulsively after it popping up in my feed a bunch over the past month and then seeing a few people in my group playing it and reviewing it positively. I don't normally play multiplayer games and something like [b] Webfishing [/b] definitely doesn't stick on my radar. 

But for some reason I was intrigued and at $5 to play I figured why not. 

I became almost [i] immediately [/i] infatuated! It's all very lo-fi from the graphics to the music and sounds to the progression system. There is nothing complicated about it, really, and much of it leaves a whole lot of room for creative interpretation. You can buy and use chalk to draw things, you can buy and use guitars and tambourines to play music, you can gamble, you can drink beer. You can upgrade your gear to catch better fish. You can find a void. 

And you can chat with people. 

I think I was pretty lucky right off because my first day playing was on Thanksgiving in the US and who I found were people mostly in a good mood, feeling generous, chatty about all the good food they were eating and cooking, and some people commiserating over their intolerable family dynamics. A few lobbies had someone playing the guitar quite well. A few lobbies had some really cool artwork. I even went to one lobby where someone gave away x10 diamond rings to everyone (which thankfully did not appear to be an actual scam of any kind). I tried a variety of lobbies and some were chattier and more active than others but overall my experience was really really good. Sure, there were some griefers but they were far outnumbered by the people who seemed to be there just to genuinely chill and relax. 

And then I started noticing a player named [b] "mack" [/b] would be in every lobby I was in. I'd join a lobby and within a minute or two [b] "mack" [/b] would join. Then leave. Then join. I started my own public lobby and [b] "mack" [/b] showed up and left about a dozen times. Nothing else notable happened but I thought it was weird. 

Then I went to the forums and was disappointed to find not only a thriving group of trolls and baiters running rampant but also a lot of community warnings of IP scraping and doxxing happening within the game. People were having save files lost or corrupted. People were being relentlessly harassed including the Developer. A lot of people were complaining about others like [b] "mack" [/b] following them around or being everywhere in lobbies and doing things like messing up save files and booting hosts/hijacking lobbies. And the further into the threads I went the more confusing and difficult to parse the accuracy and validity of any piece of information. 

Nonetheless it was super discouraging to see this new thing I was actually having a really nice time in and that [b] "mack" [/b] person could possibly culminate into some sort of real breach or issue for me. It was disheartening to see that so much of this seemed to be due to the q*eer lean this game has. I'm probably missing some nuance but that is the baseline gripe as I see it. 

I will never understand why people can't simply [u] ignore [/u] the things that are not for them or do not speak to them. It's SO easy to just go, eh, not for me so let me go spend my precious time elsewhere. Instead, people feel emboldened and righteous enough to spend that precious time making sure others feel miserable over something that hurts and disrupts no one. 

Ya'll...it's a low-budget game about hanging out and fishing. I feel a lot of pity for the terminally online emotionally fragile person who chooses to spend their time trying to hurt other people over something so pedestrian. What a frail way to spend this life. 

In any case, take all that as you will. I am hopeful that at some point the Developer will find ways to address some of this and eventually as popularity declines again [b] Webfishing [/b] will see a more consistent user base with less of this nonsense. It really is a very relaxing and fun experience I was surprised by and would like to spend more time in, I would just prefer to be in lobbies without worrying that my progress will be wiped or possibly something more nefarious. 

5/5 with a significant disclaimer right now towards griefers who aren't just drawing d*cks on the floor. Enter at your own risk.

A simple, low poly Animal Crossing like fishing game based around a cute little island with different fishing spots. There's not a huge amount of depth, simple goals to complete and it's 5 bucks which on the surface seems like a game without much to do.

But on the contrary [b]the vibe is immaculate[/b]. This game is multiplayer first and while their is no active collaborative mechanics the true joy in this game comes from basically treating the multiplayer as a chill chatroom where people shoot the shit while they fish together. The colourful aesthetic combined with the customisation options and the handful of various toys to let players be expressive and communicative makes it bizarrely easy to spend hours just standing in one place casting a rod and playing a very simply mini game to pick up fish because you're just enjoying hanging out with other people and the creators know this. There are upgrades and alike that support and allow for a much more passive form of game where you can cast your rod then go and get yourself a drink, or have a smoke or something and anything you catch on your line will wait until you come back to your keyboard to interact with the game.

 In an internet where everything is memes, gifs, zoomer brainrot and links to tiktoks this is a genuine island of tranquillity where every aspect of the game puts everybody in a calm and wholesome headspace and that means that the conversation and demeanour of the people you're sharing the island with is equally calm and wholesome. The visuals, the clothing, the overall feel of the game very much tends towards the early 30's millennial mindset who grew up failing at learning to skate, listening to pop punk and wearing chains on the belt loops of their jeans.

This game is just the best low impact way to degauss your brain in the evening and I genuinely can't wait to see where this game goes next because the devs have truly captured, not so much a gameplay loop or a mechanical system, but a genuine vibe and infused it into every aspect of the game and I want to see what else they can enviben and add to this little gem.

In sharp contrast to pretty much every other "new" game I've played in 2024, webfishing is a refreshing return to a more nostalgic time. Despite the name of the game, the primary component of webfishing that is fun is not the -fishing suffix, but the web- prefix. The fishing of the game is a brainless mouse-mashing sidequest that gives you a reason to hop onto the various servers in the first place. The true fun is the chatting and social interactions that happen in the foreground in front of the fishing. I have met so many interesting "characters" in my time on webfishing, many of whom have given me incite into who I am, what I believe in, and make me question where online gaming went wrong. In excess of 20 hours in the game, I have never had a negative interaction with a fellow fisher-person. I have had so many in-depth chats about the meaning of life, the goals we all aspire to, and what it means to be human at 3am while trying to catch the elusive Golden Ray. The Pawprint Point is mysterious and kind of creepy in the way that old flash MMOs from the 2000s could be. webfishing scratches the itch that the death of Club Penguin has left me itching for the past few years - mindless minigames while chatting with friends in a nostalgic paradise is something that I did not have on my 2024 bingo card, yet here we are. As divisive as the world seems to be, the various fishing communities on webfishing seem to be the last bastion of friendly, happy humanity. If you have even an once of child-like glee left in your body, you cannot go wrong spending $5 on a game with fishing, smoking, drinking, gambling, and your own little creature to dress and design. While the surprisingly poor performance of the game holds it back from being a truly "massive" mulitplayer online game, you will be hard pressed to find a better social avenue at 3am than a well-filled webfishing server.

[h1][b]"Man I Love Fish [MILF]"[/b][/h1]
A chill and casual experience that serves as the perfect game to play while watching shows on your second monitor. [hr][/hr][h1]Plot - Nonexistent/5[/h1] 
Webfishing doesn't have a plot whatsoever, the game throws you in, teaches you how to fish, and off you go. I think this is a positive, as there are no clear goals aside from a quest board that basically functions as achievements. 

[h1]Gameplay - 5/5[/h1] 
This is the perfect game to simply pick up and play, whether it is for a quick 10 minutes or for hours. The gameplay is simple to understand, with accessibility features for individuals who are unable to spam click when catching fish. 

A main feature of the game is the chatroom aspect of it, which makes each lobby new and interesting, and the developers added chat functions, emotes, actions, and props which work for roleplaying,as well as items that affect your character, which I think is a great addition to a chatroom game. 

Outside of fishing, players are able to purchase scratch cards in hopes to win it big, which is fun to buy and go through every so often, musical instruments which you can purchase and master playing songs with, as well as different coloured crayons which you can use to draw with. Even for those who get bored of fishing, there are still other things for you to do!

[h1]Visuals - 3.5/5[/h1] 
Personally, I am not the biggest fan of this game, however the game is intentionally designed in this manner, and the graphics give this "homely" feel in some way that I can't really describe the reasoning behind. If the player doesn't enjoy the pixellated graphics, there are graphic settings to turn off the pixellation (which I did do), and I love that the the developer decided to add that option. If you don't think the game is pixellated enough? You can go ahead and turn up the pixellation to the point that you can't tell what you're looking at anymore. 

[h1]Audio - 3/5[/h1]
I spent all of my time while playing Webfishing with the music off, so I don't have much to comment on in regards to the music. I do whoever think the SFX is not bad, but I would've liked to have volume options for specific SFX, for example, making the bell noise when a fish bites louder, rain quieter, etc. 

[h1]Replayability - 5/5[/h1]
For a game about fishing, so long as there are fish in the sea, the game has infinite replayability. It's a decent grind in order to catch all the fish in all of the rarities, not to mention the rod that costs 1 billion coins. I there's plenty of replayability in this game, after all, it's simply about fishing, as well as chatting with friends. 

[h1] Overall - 4/5[/h1] 
I enjoy Webfishing a lot, I often opened it up and fished while watching shows, and I loved fishing to purchase every item in the game, before moving on to collecting all rarities of the fish. It's the perfect game to open up and immediately jump into for a chill time, whether you intend to fish, play music, draw, gamble, or chat with others. The game has a lot of personality with the flavour text for items and fish, as well as cosmetics, which I think made the game more unique and likeable.

This makes this game possible to experience like the old days where you'd figure something out and hold onto that precious information so you can tell everyone at school the next day.

It has no meta, there is no right way to play it, no stress involved whatsoever. It's just fun to find out things by exploring and experimenting.

The community (AKA randos that join your lobby if you choose to leave it open) so far has been wonderful. There are no mechanics designed so that others can ruin your fun, so they just join to roam around and fish together.

> If you have friends, it is an absolute blast.

> If you have no friends, it is ALSO an absolute blast.

PS: you can play the guitar in this game, and for a game about fishing, oddly enough it has one of the best guitar playing systems in any game I have ever seen. Me and my other guitar-playing friends have fun just trying to play chords or simple riffs.

This could honestly become my GOTY for 2024.

I don't usually review games, but hey, I reached this many hours in this one; might as well.

The Good:
-Meet strangers and barely get to know one another just like in real life circumstances but instead of people you want to avoid it's little small creatures out to fish the day away.
-Become enthralled by the sheer amount of fulfillment a silly journal asks of you that's clearly daunting at first until you realize it's just fishing, fishing, and more fishing.
-Take a break from fishing and partake in silly activities on the side such as metal detecting, punching people with a boxing glove, or strumming away on a guitar.
-Aimlessly wander around the Void.
-Swap stories with other players about your in-game or out of game experiences like the neet or 9-5 worker you are.
-Engage in thrilling fishing minigame interactivity that you're either too numb to complain when you have a second keybind for mashing ( \ ) or literally need an autoclicker that's built into the game because you're unable to mash like a pro.
-Doodle on the dirt like the artist you want to be, reminiscent even of Jet Set Radio Future's Custom Graffiti Maker with the Chalk system, made better using Freecam together with CTRL and SHIFT to adjust your chalk sizes.
-Support your fellow WebFishers as you lobby hop your way over the course of the day to hang out with new people as you feel the want to, when you want to.
-Host a Lobby when you want to settle down, and let some new people into your life. (Optionally, private lobbies exist for just friend interactions as well.)

The Bad:
-Game's 100% unmoderated, considering I've been called a snowflake by a few groomer types in the game take this as your warning that you need to keep yourself at least somewhat aware of the lobbies you get involved with.
-Game definitely has groomers in it. Hell, I've been called one for simply giving tips and advice to new players.
-Modded can be a double edged sword; irresponsible players can and WILL slow down vanilla player lobbies without a care in the world. Modded players are going so far as to push for mods that autokick players from their lobbies if they don't have a similar mod installed, as well. 
-A specific mod enables gooners to post porn in lobbies, a la TF2 spray style. It's very clear some lobbies are meant for this; but I've sadly encountered it in many where the lobbies were by no means meant for that.
-If you don't have some optimization mods, the game quickly begins a mad descent into a memory leak that simply slows it more and more. It's been in the game since day 1 and was never fixed, with a handful of mods slightly taming it, but you'll still want to restart the game after long sessions (or short if your PC isn't quite up to date) to ensure it doesn't lag out.

The Ugly:
-Dev was supposedly doxxed over this game's mitigated LGBT+ support or some nonsense. I personally don't care for any statements the community has to make, the first time I ever read anything from the dev was a tweet they made saying "You could definitely have sex in this game" which clearly aimed the direction the community has gone for from time to time. Otherwise, the Dev is currently MIA and likely will not give any more updates to the game in the future. Modding appears to be all the game has right now.
-With the last update, the lobby lists have been seeing less and less overall populated listings; this is because vanilla clients are set to specific areas of the world. Modded clients can see everywhere and nearby, instead of just a specific region. This means vanilla players have technically seen a decline in lobby activity, from other vanilla players. The latest bug for vanilla players ensuring the newest join on a lobby has their name stay blank, doesn't help either, though there is a mod to fix that.

Conclusion: 
My small graffiti styled sprays of the Team Skull logo and the sprite that matches my pfp are how most know me in this game, and that may fade away given the game's not got much left to give, even with modding added in the mix. It's always nice to swap stories with someone every here and there, but lobbies are slowly turning into the chaotically out of place VRChat atmosphere and I'm not here for that. But I sure did 100% the game and then keep going for a good while. You know what that means!

This low-poly, fishing, chatroom game is a very chill game that anyone can immediately jump into and start playing. The relaxing visuals and old school nostalgia-inducing music tracks add a lot to that feeling of fishing into a particularly niche yet relaxing corner of the internet. I've gotten far more enjoyment out of this game than the last Animal Crossing game even though this game really is just "fishing" (this has been my elevator pitch to friends to try the game). There's a few more small activities that really elevate the social aspect of this game, such as drawing chalk with friends, boxing your buds, playing music with the in-game guitar, and exploring out-of-bounds. lamedeveloper, the developer working on Webfishing, even incorporated an out-of-bounds area and made it into a real and intended mechanic, which is pretty extraordinary and extremely cool to see from a developer. Embracing community-made urban legends and enhancing their game is something more developers should use to add content to their games.

I am a bit saddened by how easy it was to exploit this game and ban users from their own servers as well as corrupt saves, but I can give the benefit of the doubt since I'm sure this developer wasn't ready for this game to be as popular as it has (just be sure to make save backups and don't accept mail from suspicious people). One thing that actually does ruin the mood a bit is removing flag linking. Before, you could get to CRAZY out-of-bounds areas and place two flags to link them together so you can get all of your friends from spawn to join you in one of those areas (see my screenshots for a few examples). I had an absolute metric ton of fun exploring out-of-bounds areas with friends. However, flag linking was intentionally or unintentionally removed and due to how the new out-of-bounds area was created, it is A LOT harder to get yourself and friends out-of-bounds to the areas that you could go to previously.

Overall, this game is very very very well worth that $5 cost seeing as how many hours I've gotten out of this game with fishing, shooting the shit, and talking to deranged psychopaths at 3 AM.

Webfishing is a game that in my opinion ended up being both underrated and overrated all at once. While I think it definitely deserved the praise it got during its peak popularity, I think a lot of people sleep on the fact that, at its core, webfishing is an extremely solid experience- even now, a year+ later.

It's a great way to socialize, even if you usually struggle with social interactions. Webfishing makes it easy to make friends, and even easier to hang out with already existing ones. That being said, webfishing is also a wonderful experience to play solo. I experienced both ends of it while 100%'ing it and can with my full chest say that neither one is a superior experience. They both have their charm and the game could easily appeal to you regardless of if your playstyle is to be silly with your mates, or if you want a serious solo completionist experience. 

Webfishing, aside from catch rates that can be rightout infuriating at times (despite being sheer RNG, I know, I just- like everyone else playing this game, am salty some fish took stupidly long to catch), is extremely soothing and cozy. With nice timeless graphics, easy to grasp mechanics and a collectors book that is both big enough to be challanging, while being small enough to feel do-able. 

This game allows you to have upbeat fun and yap people's ears off, unwind and take a chill pill, or sulk and cope with things outside of your control that might be going on in your life, and as such, I can highly recommend it to anyone that might be considering or hesitant to buy it.

At worst, you find the game tideous and don't play more than a few hours, at best? You make memories with people that will stick with you, get an outlet, and a way to escape the short attention span feeding nonsense that is today's society. If you're hesitant, take the plunge! I promise you, you won't regret it.
